text.p: Shares of state-controlled Bank Negara Indonesia traded heavily and made significant gains on Thursday on the Jakarta exchange on continued speculation that the firm would book higher income in 1996, brokers said.
"Both foreign and local buying interest in the stock has remained high since last week," an analyst with a foreign brokerage firm said.
By mid-afternoon on Wednesday, the bank was up 75 rupiah to 1,625 rupiah and topped the active list with 67.1 million shares traded.
The analyst said this was mostly on expectations that the company would book higher income in 1996 following rumour that its profit would be 10 percent over its IPO forecast of 326 billion rupiah.
"Assuming it's true, investors should re-evaluate their forecast for 1997. Based on the 1997 forecast, the current PER (price earnings ratio) is cheap," he said.

Brokers also said there was speculation that a management fee of four percent the bank had paid from its profits to the government no longer applied since the bank became a listed company last November 25.
Shares of the blue chip bank have also traded actively on market talk that Morgan Stanley would include the bank in its capital index starting on February 15.
